review_markdown:
The backend S1 contract is coherent within its bounded scope. Three delivery-contract gaps need repair before dispatch: stage the test setup permissions explicitly, assign post-D1 machine continuation work, and distinguish the JSON-RPC library from the line-protocol binary.

Independently verified HEAD `6fb4aeee7441ffc0fd64e5c015697c4cdd656491`, branch `feat/monster-hp-d8`, every original artifact hash, all 344 individual baseline hashes, and recomputed digest `567aed72fc97273ac4209afe92decbd5175e8e576ec7b5933bdb14c871e4e707`. All seven pinned C file hashes, Git blob identities and supplied snapshots matched retrieval at authority commit `16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4`. Accepted identity/configuration evidence was hash-verified and reused without reopening those implementations.

Bounded source reads support the proposed complete direct-carried index, optional captured generational token, class-before-identity validation, precharge refusal/cancellation, and delegation to the existing selected wand behavior. Index-only requests correctly mean the current snapshot. C getobj retry/menu/count/hands/queue behavior remains distinct from backend refusal and explicitly deferred. Charge/backfire/direction/preflight conformance remains successor work.

Reviewed all eight fixture groups, legacy serialization/parser constraints, native save/default/omission requirements, pack/schema preservation, three ActionArgs setup sites, two enum-test setups, and all ten declared surfaces. The proposed dependency graph is acyclic when closure_update is applied, but its machine continuation ownership is incomplete. D1 explicitly requires native resumable prepare/charged AwaitDirection/continue, pending save/oldload, terminal actor and duplicate-continuation handling before frontend acceptance.

Graph tools were unavailable; used bounded known-path source reads. No implementation, file edits, nested agents, Cargo/tests, compilation, preprocessing, C/custom C evaluator/Lua execution, commits or golden changes occurred. Existing dirty ledger state was preserved. This review accepts no implementation or aggregate closure; all 53 families remain open.

findings.trigger: Dispatching S1 using the ready packet's setup permissions and exact six-file allowance.
findings.evidence: contract.json#/children/0/files allows exactly six files and excludes crates/nethacked-agent/tests/protocol_tests.rs. However, #/allowed_existing_setup/protocol_test permits modifying mcp_step_enum_matches_accepted_actions there without assigning that permission to S1-M. ready-packet.md also presents both enum-test setup changes together. Current STEP_ACTIONS has neither new name; its advertisement changes belong S1-M.
findings.consequence: The implementer cannot determine whether the protocol test change is authorized now or deferred. Applying all advertised setup edits during S1 violates its file boundary.
findings.repair: Assign each existing setup edit to a named stage. Keep the three full ActionArgs field initializations within S1's six files; explicitly place the protocol enum setup change in S1-M when STEP_ACTIONS changes. State when the command enum adaptation occurs, and preserve both existing tests' loops/assertions and old-action inputs.

findings.trigger: Accepting S1-F's all-ten-surface exit after D1.
findings.evidence: contract.json#/children/1 depends only on S1 and expressly makes no charged continuation claim. #/children/2 permits only TUI/browser files while claiming prompting/cancellation across all ten surfaces. #/frontends/3 and /4 require machine prepare/continue paths after D1. D1's required native continuation is explicit, but no successor assigns the subsequent MCP/JSON-RPC/GraphQL/WASM/Python adapter and transcript changes with corresponding file ownership and dependency edges.
findings.consequence: The graph is acyclic but does not completely allocate the advertised machine continuation exit. Completing the listed S1-M, native D1 and six-file S1-F scopes could still leave machine surfaces unable to resume charged direction selection.
findings.repair: Explicitly assign post-D1 machine continuation integration and its fixtures to a successor with the required adapter/test files. This may be an expanded S1-F scope or another concrete child depending on S1-M and D1. Make S1-F/A1 consume that accepted evidence, retain the existing C1/P1/B1/D1 ordering, and keep backend S1 independent of the unresolved interfaces.

findings.trigger: Checking parser transport errors and frontend coverage for the combined JSON-RPC library/bin surface.
findings.evidence: contract.json#/parser/transport_errors specifies JSONRPC INVALID_PARAMS -32602, and #/frontends/4 requires that envelope while naming agent/jsonrpc.rs as owner. The library maps parser errors to -32602 at crates/nethacked-agent/src/jsonrpc.rs:45. The separate crates/nethacked-agent/src/bin/jsonrpc.rs:35 returns a flat {error: ...} response and does not call the library dispatcher; it is absent from S1-M's file list.
findings.consequence: The packet's transport expectation is false for the binary, and its combined owner mapping can omit binary inventory/continuation integration despite claiming coverage of that route.
findings.repair: Document the library and binary subroutes separately within the declared surface: preserve -32602 for the library and the existing flat error envelope for the binary, both before session.step. Explicitly assign binary adapter work and regression evidence to the appropriate successor. Do not change its protocol implicitly during S1.
